quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol affect blood alcohol concentration?

options.text: It has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee cannot lower your blood alcohol concentration. It may keep you awake, but it cannot change how much alcohol is in your blood or make you sober.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Always, even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
Only if the pedestrian signals the driver to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or crossing without paying attention.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, which vehicle has the right-of-way if both arrive at the same time?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control, you must yield to a vehicle approaching from your right.

questions.question: What should a worried, nervous, angry, or crying driver do?

options.text: Drive normally since emotions do not affect driving.
Drive faster because they are more aware.
Calm down and focus before starting the engine.
Call a friend while driving to feel better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving safely. Your mind is focused on your feelings instead of the road. Calm down and get your mind clear before you start driving.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, is nighttime driving safer or more dangerous?

options.text: It is easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Nighttime driving is more dangerous than daytime driving. It is harder to see in the dark. Headlights from other vehicles can temporarily blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: What is important to do before turning left?

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should a driver of a small vehicle expect when passing a large vehicle?

options.text: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create powerful wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Be ready to steer correctly when approaching or passing large vehicles traveling at high speeds.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: To avoid distractions from other vehicles.
To have time to react to unexpected situations.
To keep traffic moving at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: To have time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space around your vehicle gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes. This is the best way to stay safe.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign warn drivers about?
questions.correctAnswerText: Existing or possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or dangerous conditions. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: How can you prevent another vehicle from hitting your car from behind?

options.text: Drive faster than surrounding traffic to increase the distance between you and the vehicle behind.
Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic.
Drive slower than surrounding traffic to have better control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Match the speed of surrounding traffic within the legal speed limit. Driving with traffic flow helps prevent rear-end collisions and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon
questions.explanation: Stop signs are octagonal (eight-sided). Only stop signs use this shape. All eight-sided signs mean you must come to a complete stop before going forward.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. Always slow down when approaching railroad tracks. Trains cannot move out of the way, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Stop and check for police cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says not to. When turning, you must let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection cross first.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, where should your car be positioned?

options.text: Near the center of the street
Close to the left side of the street
Close to the right side of the street
Past the center of the intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cut across other lanes of traffic.

questions.question: On average, how long does it take for your body to process one 12-ounce can of beer?
questions.correctAnswerText: One hour
questions.explanation: It takes about one hour to process one drink. This time can be longer depending on various factors. The safest choice is not to drive after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal to tell them when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming cars and slow down to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming cars and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when someone is passing you on the left. Look for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the other driver can pass and return to the right lane easily.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and proceed carefully at an intersection?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed carefully, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?
questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase how far your car travels before stopping and how severe a crash will be. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits in a crash.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: The fastest and slowest speeds you are allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest and slowest speeds you are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the legal maximum and minimum speeds for that road. These limits are for ideal conditions. You must drive slower when weather or road conditions are poor.
